stem:
Pallavi asks whether $(x+3)^{2}=x^{2}+6x+9$ is an identity.

Which claim correctly decides?

options.text: Name the left-hand side only, without comparing a simplified right-hand side.
Matching one trial value on the left-hand side is what creates an identity.
Expand and simplify both sides; they agree for every permitted $x$, so the equality is an identity.
It is an identity because the trial $x=1$ made both sides equal.

teacher.key_rationale: An identity holds for all permitted values. Expanding (x+3)^2 gives x^2+6x+9, matching the other side generally; a single trial is not enough.
